[ASSISTANT_SAID] Maca root: Grown in the high Andes of Peru, nutritionally-dense, high in vitamins and minerals, known for energy-boosting properties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Camu camu: A berry native to the Amazon rainforest, anti-inflammatory, high in vitamin C, often used to boost the immune system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Chia seeds: Originally from Mexico and Central America, packed with nutrients including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and antioxidants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yerba mate: A plant native to Argentina, Paraguay, and Brazil, a natural source of caffeine, known for energy-boosting properties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lucuma: A fruit native to the Andean region, high in beta-carotene, fiber, and antioxidants, often used to sweeten desserts and smoothies.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Quinoa salad recipe: Cook quinoa, mix with parsley, tomatoes, cucumbers, red onions, and dressing; serve cold.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Acai bowl recipe: Blend frozen acai berries, frozen bananas, and almond milk; top with sliced bananas, fresh berries, granola, and honey.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Maca hot chocolate recipe: Heat almond milk, whisk in cocoa powder, maca powder, and maple syrup; serve hot.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Camu camu smoothie recipe: Blend frozen bananas, frozen pineapple, frozen spinach, fresh orange juice, and camu camu powder; enjoy cold.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Chia seed pudding recipe: Mix chia seeds, almond milk, and maple syrup; let sit in the fridge until thick; top with fresh fruit, nuts, and honey.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yerba mate chicken marinade recipe: Brew strong yerba mate tea, mix with olive oil, garlic, and oregano; marinate chicken breasts for at least an hour before cooking.
